nodes.label: release.lua Compensation Script
nodes.rationale: Releases only when this order's reservation holds the user's unit, so a repeat call or a stale event for an older order cannot release a newer one.

nodes.label: LocalStack
nodes.rationale: Rejected: since March 2026 the image requires an account and auth token, and the free Hobby tier is limited to non-commercial use.

nodes.label: Context Retrieval Policy
nodes.rationale: Agents retrieve the smallest amount of information necessary, escalating from graph.json to ast-grep, rtk, source files, then repository-wide search.

nodes.label: System Invariants
nodes.rationale: Rules that must never be broken: no oversell, one active order per user, atomic reserve, idempotent compensation, conditional saga transitions, fail closed.

nodes.label: Scope Cut Rule
nodes.rationale: Cut from the end of the plan when time is short. Phase 2 concurrency tests and verify.ts are never cut because they prove correctness.

nodes.label: Phase 0: Walking Skeleton
nodes.rationale: A hello-world request crosses every final component, proving wiring, networking, configuration, tests and stress tooling before business logic exists.

nodes.label: AOF everysec Durability Window
nodes.rationale: Accepts losing about 1 s of reservations on restart for local simplicity. Production would use Sentinel or a managed replica with WAIT.

nodes.label: Conditional Status Transitions
nodes.rationale: Optimistic concurrency: when zero rows update, the event is replanned against the current status because it may still owe a side effect such as a refund.

nodes.label: Durable Release (released_at)
nodes.rationale: The status commits first and released_at is set after the release succeeds, so a crash or Redis outage delays a release but cannot lose it.

nodes.label: Fail Closed on Redis Outage
nodes.rationale: Purchases return 503 rather than risk overselling when Redis is unavailable.

nodes.label: Floci for Local SQS
nodes.rationale: MIT-licensed and needs no account or token, so reviewers can run the project without signing up. Risk from its youth is limited by a pinned tag, plain SQS API use and contract tests.

nodes.label: MessageBus Abstraction
nodes.rationale: Code depends on publish and subscribe rather than the SQS SDK, with SqsBus and InMemoryBus adapters, so brokers can be swapped and unit tests need no I/O.

nodes.label: Orchestrated Saga
nodes.rationale: One state machine in the orchestrator is easier to read, test and explain than events bouncing between services.

nodes.label: Purchase Decision Made in Redis
nodes.rationale: Redis runs scripts one at a time, so a single O(1) Lua script is linearizable with no locks and no database row contention.

nodes.label: Redis TIME as Authoritative Clock
nodes.rationale: Using Redis TIME inside the script makes every API replica agree on the time regardless of host clock drift.

nodes.label: Per-Replica soldOut Flag
nodes.rationale: Short-circuits with 410 and skips Redis after sell-out to absorb the thundering herd, re-checked every second.

nodes.label: Redis Stream as Outbox
nodes.rationale: Writing the reservation and its event in one script means neither can exist without the other, so no two-phase commit is needed.

nodes.label: Deterministic Failure Rate Defaults
nodes.rationale: The compose stack defaults mock failure rates to 0 so e2e and stress scenarios are deterministic. Compensation is exercised by recreating the stack with a non-zero rate.

nodes.label: Rootless Podman via DOCKER_HOST
nodes.rationale: The docker CLI with the Compose plugin talks to the Podman socket. podman-compose is unsupported because it lacks up --wait.
